@graph.name: How to run pre-token-launch PR before a TGE
@graph.description: The 25-step, five-phase PR sequence to run over an eight-week run-up to a token generation event: foundation and positioning, narrative and assets, media and KOL outreach, launch week, and post-TGE follow-through.

step.name: Foundation and positioning (T-8 to T-6 weeks)

itemListElement.name: Lock the one-sentence token thesis
itemListElement.text: Define what the token does, why it matters now, and who it is for. Every downstream asset, pitch and KOL brief inherits this sentence, so write it first.

itemListElement.name: Map the forcing events and build the calendar backward
itemListElement.text: Pin the TGE date, exchange listings, mainnet and named partnerships, then schedule every push back from them. A launch with no dated hook gets passed on.

itemListElement.name: Set the regulatory posture per market and loop counsel early
itemListElement.text: Decide what you can and cannot say about price, returns and utility in each jurisdiction, then write the messaging inside those lines.

itemListElement.name: Build the single-source fact sheet
itemListElement.text: One document covering tokenomics, supply, vesting, use of proceeds, audit status and named investors, so the facts never drift between outlets.

itemListElement.name: Agree the scorecard now, not impressions
itemListElement.text: Set named target outlets, inbound and pipeline signal, launch sentiment and AI-citation presence as the definition of winning before the work starts.

step.name: Narrative and assets (T-6 to T-4 weeks)

itemListElement.name: Write the launch as a category story, not a token ad
itemListElement.text: Anchor the launch to a real market shift the token addresses, because reporters underwrite a trend with a protagonist, not a coin with a price.

itemListElement.name: Prepare the founder as a quotable voice
itemListElement.text: Give the founder three to five message points, a media-training pass and a byline or Op-Ed drafted for launch week.

itemListElement.name: Produce the press kit
itemListElement.text: Assemble a logo pack, headshots, product screenshots, a 60-second explainer and an embargoed release so a reporter can publish without a follow-up email.

itemListElement.name: Draft and approve crisis holding statements
itemListElement.text: Pre-approve language for predictable failure modes like a price dump, an exploit rumor or a listing delay, before the hour you need it.

itemListElement.name: Build the on-site GEO and AEO layer
itemListElement.text: Ship a launch page with a front-loaded answer, FAQ content, named statistics and consistent entity signals so AI engines assemble the answer from your page.

step.name: Media and KOL outreach (T-4 to T-2 weeks)

itemListElement.name: Tier the outlet list by name
itemListElement.text: Name the crypto-native desks, the regional outlets your buyers read and the one or two mainstream targets that genuinely fit, then brief on outlets not logos.

itemListElement.name: Open embargoed conversations 10 to 14 days out
itemListElement.text: Offer a clean exclusive to the single best-fit outlet, then a coordinated embargo to the rest, respecting the embargo discipline tier-1 desks expect.

itemListElement.name: Contract a vetted KOL wave timed to the window
itemListElement.text: Book a disclosure-compliant KOL wave matched to the token thesis and sequenced to the launch, never a generic buy fired at random.

itemListElement.name: Line up regional placements in parallel
itemListElement.text: Cover the overnight regional windows in Korea, Japan, the Chinese-language market and India, because TGE news often breaks for one region overnight.

itemListElement.name: Prepare partner and investor co-marketing
itemListElement.text: Get quotes approved, partner channels briefed and assets shared so launch-day amplification is one click for them rather than a scramble for you.

itemListElement.name: Confirm the embargo time in every reporter's timezone
itemListElement.text: Send final assets 24 to 48 hours ahead so nobody is waiting on a file when the clock hits zero.

itemListElement.name: Sequence the day on a single timeline
itemListElement.text: Break the exclusive first, follow with re-reports, fire regional and KOL waves on schedule, and have the founder post within minutes of the break.

itemListElement.name: Staff a launch-day war room
itemListElement.text: Watch coverage, sentiment and on-chain chatter in real time so a misreport or wrong number is caught and corrected fast.

itemListElement.name: Keep the crisis statements loaded
itemListElement.text: If price moves hard or an exploit rumor starts, respond from the pre-approved language within the hour, because speed and consistency beat a late perfect statement.

itemListElement.name: Capture everything as it lands
itemListElement.text: Log every placement, screenshot and quote in real time, both for the final report and as proof assets you reuse for months.

itemListElement.name: Publish the founder Op-Ed within 72 hours
itemListElement.text: Put the durable founder asset out while attention is highest and the category is still listening.

itemListElement.name: Convert the launch into durable assets
itemListElement.text: Turn the launch into a case study, a teardown and FAQ content that keep earning AI citations long after the news cycle ends.

itemListElement.name: Run the regional follow-through
itemListElement.text: Ship localized re-reports and KOL recaps in the markets that woke up after the US window, so no region is left on a single launch-day hit.

itemListElement.name: Report against the scorecard
itemListElement.text: Report placement quality in named outlets, inbound and pipeline, launch sentiment and AI-citation presence, with reach as a supporting line.

itemListElement.name: Schedule the next forcing event
itemListElement.text: Put the next dated hook on the calendar before this one cools, because sequenced launches compound where one-offs do not.

Pre-Token Launch PR Checklist 2026

mainEntity.name: How far before a TGE should PR start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six to twelve weeks, with eight as the standard run-up. Pre-token-launch PR is sequencing work: positioning, the fact sheet, the narrative, the KOL wave and embargo prep all build on each other, so the founders with the most runway get the strongest result. If you have fewer than six weeks, do not compress all five phases. Pick the two that move your launch most, usually the single-source fact sheet and the embargo sequence, and run those well.

mainEntity.name: What goes in a pre-token-launch press kit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single-source fact sheet (tokenomics, supply, vesting, use of proceeds, audit status, named investors), an embargoed press release, a logo pack, founder headshots, product screenshots, and a 60-second explainer. The test is whether a reporter could publish an accurate story from the kit alone without a follow-up email. Everything traces back to one fact sheet so the numbers never drift between outlets.

mainEntity.name: How do you keep token launch PR compliant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Decide the regulatory posture for each target market before you write a word, loop counsel in early, and keep messaging inside what you can defensibly say about price, returns and utility in that jurisdiction. Draft crisis holding statements for predictable events like a price dump or a listing delay and get them approved in advance. Compliance handled as a constraint up front is far cheaper than a correction after launch.

mainEntity.name: Do KOLs still matter for token launches in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only as a vetted wave matched to the token thesis and sequenced to the launch window, never a generic buy fired at random. KOLs and regional outlets cover the overnight windows in Korea, Japan, Vietnam and India where Web3 liquidity and community concentrate, and they must run with proper disclosure. The point is coordination with the earned-media push, not volume.

mainEntity.name: How do you make a token launch visible in AI search?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build an on-site GEO and AEO layer before launch: a page with a front-loaded answer, FAQ content, named statistics and consistent entity signals so AI engines can extract and cite it. AI Overviews appear on roughly 48 percent of US Google queries in 2026 and most of those searches end without a click, so being cited inside the AI answer matters as much as the click. Earned media with quotable, citable data feeds those brand citations, which is why steps 8 and 10 pair the press kit with the AI-search layer.
